Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Glyphic test: separating AP-1 the writer from AP-1 the reader with acute degron depletion
ideas.description: Inspired by "glyphic" (a mark that outlasts the hand that cut it), tag FOS/JUN family members with auxin or dTAG degrons and deplete them either during a transient stimulus or only after washout, then assay ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN accessibility at AP-1 enhancers and the amplitude/latency of a second response. If memory requires AP-1 only during encoding but survives its post-stimulus removal, AP-1 writes the mark; if the potentiated second response collapses whenever AP-1 is absent, AP-1 is continuously read out rather than stored.

ideas.title: Semicolon experiment: AP-1 bookmarking across the mitotic break
ideas.description: A semicolon interrupts a sentence without severing it, which is the structural question for memory through cell division: image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN/ATF in live mitotic cells (plus mitotic CUT&RUN and H3S10ph-matched controls) to quantify retention on condensed chromatin at specific enhancers. Pair this with stimulating mother cells, tracking single daughters by lineage imaging, and testing whether potentiated re-induction is inherited and whether it is lost when bookmarking is disrupted by an AP-1 DNA-binding-deficient or mitosis-evicted mutant.

ideas.title: Hornbook grammar: an MPRA of AP-1 motif syntax under two-hit stimulation
ideas.description: Like a hornbook, where a few letters in defined arrangements generate the whole lexicon, build a synthetic reporter library systematically varying TRE/CRE motif number, spacing, affinity, and flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, CEBP, nucleosome-positioning sequences), and measure each variant's output after a single stimulus versus a stimulus-washout-restimulus protocol. This directly reads out which cis-grammars confer the hallmark of memory—faster, larger, or lower-threshold second responses—rather than mere responsiveness.

ideas.title: Weighing the engram: single-cell dose-response-to-memory transfer functions
ideas.description: Treating AP-1 as a "graduator" that meters an analog quantity, use live-cell endogenous FOS/JUN translational reporters with a dynamic transcriptional readout to measure, in the same cell, the integrated AP-1 activity during a first graded stimulus and the magnitude of the subsequent response weeks-to-hours later. Fitting the resulting transfer function distinguishes graded (analog, dose-proportional) memory from digital latching and reveals whether cell-to-cell variability in memory is predicted by AP-1 level or by a downstream bistable element.

ideas.title: Undo: targeted erasure and decay-rate measurement at individual AP-1 enhancers
ideas.description: Taking "undo" as the operative test of any memory claim, use dCas9-LSD1/HDAC/DNMT3A tethering, enhancer deletion, or CRISPRi tiling at specific stimulus-induced AP-1-bound enhancers after the stimulus is gone, and ask whether the potentiated second response is selectively erased while the naive response is preserved. In parallel, measure memory half-life across a washout time course with and without proliferation arrest to determine whether decay is set by chromatin turnover, dilution by cell division, or active removal.
